```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# PCAdapt

```{r}
# Convert VCF file to pcadapt format

vcf2pcadapt("SNP.TRS6dp10g5mafMIp9g95nDNAmaf052A.recode.vcf", output = "tmp.pcadapt6_8500snps", allele.sep = c("/", "|"))

filename6_8500snps <- read.pcadapt("tmp.pcadapt6_8500snps", type = "pcadapt")
```

```{r}
# Choosing the number K of Principal Components
# We start off with a large number of PCs
x6_8500snps <- pcadapt(input = filename6_8500snps, K = 20)
```

```{r}
# Plot the likelihoods using a screeplot
plot(x6_8500snps, option = "screeplot")
```

```{r}
# Plotting likelihoods again, but with 10 Principal Components
plot(x6_8500snps, option = "screeplot", K = 10)
```

```{r}
# Create population designations minus NAR, NAR2, GHP
poplist.names6 <- c(rep("BAR", 10),rep("BIS", 10),rep("GB", 10), rep("KIC", 10),rep("MCD", 10), rep("PVD", 10))
```

```{r}
# Score Plot
# Plot the first two PCs
plot(x6_8500snps, option = "scores", pop = poplist.names6)
```

```{r}
# PCA plot with PCs 3 and 4
plot(x6_8500snps, option = "scores", i = 3, j = 4, pop = poplist.names6)
```

```{r}
#evaluating LD in dataset - looking to see if loading are clustered in certain genomic regions (following https://bcm-uga.github.io/pcadapt/articles/pcadapt.html#f--linkage-disequilibrium-ld-thinning)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
for (i in 1:4)
  plot(x6_8500snps$loadings[, i], pch = 19, cex = .3, ylab = paste0("Loadings PC", i))
```

Top left, PC1, is determined by one (maybe 2) genomic regions, also likely still an inversion.

```{r}
# performing SNP thinning in order to compute PCs
res6_8500snps <- pcadapt(filename6_8500snps, K = 20, LD.clumping = list(size = 5000, thr = 0.1))
plot(res6_8500snps, option = "screeplot")
```

```{r}
# Score Plot
# Plot the first two PCs
plot(res6_8500snps, option = "scores", pop = poplist.names6)
```

```{r}
# PCA plot with PCs 3 and 4
plot(res6_8500snps, option = "scores", i = 3, j = 4, pop = poplist.names6)
```

```{r}
res6_8500snps <- pcadapt(filename6_8500snps, K = 5, LD.clumping = list(size = 5000, thr = 0.1))
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
for (i in 1)
  plot(res6_8500snps$loadings[, i], pch = 19, cex = .3, ylab = paste0("Loadings PC", i))
```

```{r}
plot(res6_8500snps)
```

```{r}
res6_8500snps$singular.values
```

```{r}
# Create Q-Q Plot
plot(res6_8500snps, option = "qqplot", threshold = 0.1)
```


```{r}
# Look at p-value distribution 
plot(res6_8500snps, option = "stat.distribution")
```

#### Assigning an alpha value

```{r}
library(qvalue) # transforms p-values into q-values.
```

```{r}
qval6_8500snps <- qvalue(res6_8500snps$pvalues)$qvalues
alpha6_8500snps <- 0.1 # expected false discovery rate lower than 1% - raised from 0.05
```

#### Save Outliers

```{r}
outliers6_8500snps <- which(qval6_8500snps < alpha6_8500snps)
outliers6_8500snps
```
